rows.text: The cache stores the last 256 responses. When it fills, the oldest response is removed.
rows.reason: Concrete technical description; the passive clause is useful and clear.

rows.text: I missed the bus, so I walked home. The rain started two blocks from my door.
rows.reason: Ordinary personal narrative without ornamental framing.

rows.text: The flag disables email alerts, not audit logging. Audit entries are still written for every failed login.
rows.reason: The contrast distinguishes two behaviors that a reader could confuse.

rows.text: Bring a passport, a signed consent form, and the receipt. The clerk checks all three before issuing the permit.
rows.reason: Three items are concrete requirements, not a decorative rhetorical triad.

rows.text: The phrase "a vibrant tapestry of possibilities" appears twice in the draft. Delete the first occurrence and replace the second with the actual options.
rows.reason: The author discusses and quotes a cliché rather than endorsing it.

rows.text: In the ever-evolving landscape of modern technology, it is important to note that teams must embrace innovation to unlock their full potential.
rows.reason: Generic scene-setting, throat-clearing, and an unsupported promise replace a concrete claim.

findings.title: Generic era opener
findings.question: Does the prose open with generic era framing such as in today's rapidly changing world rather than name a specific relevant circumstance?
findings.guidance: Lead with the actual claim or the specific circumstance already provided.

findings.title: Importance windup
findings.question: Does the prose announce that a fact is important to note or worth noting before stating it, where deleting that announcement would preserve the information?
findings.guidance: State the fact directly; retain any substantive reason it matters.

rows.text: This calendar is not just a calendar. It is a revolution in how we imagine time, a bold testament to the limitless power of human possibility.
rows.reason: Inflated negative parallelism and grandiose significance have no concrete support.

findings.title: Stock breakthrough claim
findings.question: Does pushes the boundaries, unlocks the full potential, game changer, or paradigm shift praise a development without identifying the specific new capability or change?
findings.guidance: Describe the actual change from the supplied evidence or remove the stock praise.

findings.title: Generic step-forward claim
findings.question: Does a step forward or a step toward framing praise progress without saying what capability or outcome actually changed?
findings.guidance: State the concrete change, or remove the progress framing.

rows.text: Absolutely, that is a fantastic question! Here is a polished paragraph for your report. Let me know if you would like me to make it more engaging.
rows.reason: Assistant-to-user chatter has leaked into the intended prose artifact.

findings.title: Generic reader flattery
findings.question: Does the prose lavish generic praise on the reader or their question, such as absolutely brilliant question, without a specific substantive assessment?
findings.guidance: Remove the generic praise and answer or assess the substance directly.

rows.text: Experts widely agree that this approach will transform the industry, and many observers have highlighted its profound implications for the future.
rows.reason: Unidentified authorities carry sweeping claims without attributable evidence.

findings.title: Unnamed authority
findings.question: Does the prose attribute a claim to studies, experts, observers, or researchers without identifying any source in the supplied text, excluding explicitly anonymized participants?
findings.guidance: Identify the source if available; otherwise flag the missing attribution instead of manufacturing one.

findings.title: Sweeping consensus appeal
findings.question: Does the text appeal to what everyone knows or what every expert teaches as authority without specifying a source or relevant scope?
findings.guidance: Remove the sweeping appeal or give the scope already supported; do not invent a citation.

findings.title: Generic step-forward claim
findings.question: Does a step forward or a step toward framing praise progress without saying what capability or outcome actually changed?
findings.guidance: State the concrete change, or remove the progress framing.

rows.text: We conducted an investigation into the utilization of a methodology for the facilitation of the identification of errors.
rows.reason: Nominalizations and inflated wording obscure a simple research action.

findings.title: Inflated corporate wording
findings.question: Does the prose use operationalize, functionality, or methodology where a simpler verb, feature, or method would carry the same specific meaning?
findings.guidance: Choose the simpler equivalent only when no technical distinction is lost.
